A standalone SymPy checker evaluates these identities and one exact example; the infinite assertions are proved analytically, not by testing.

originality.rationale: The motivating full text gives all-strength existence but only weak/strong diagonal analytic uniqueness; its two-parameter plots are numerical. The diagonal restriction is a strict special case and is not counted as independent novelty; the novel claim is the full independent-parameter classification and distinct one-axis limits. Classical SIRC is a zero-feedback specialization. Structured searches found no stronger covering theorem; absence of hits is not a proof of novelty, and inaccessible older full-text literature remains a genuine residual risk.
residual_risks: Full text of Casagrandi et al. (2006) was not inspected; only abstract/bibliographic evidence was available. Its zero-feedback model is not expected to dominate the two-feedback theorem, but no whole-document noncoverage is claimed.
Unindexed or not-yet-public mathematical research, including possible independent reductions, cannot be ruled out.
The diagonal specialization alone is not counted as novel; the claim requires unequal independent feedback strengths.

value.rationale: Independent immune-waning and immune-escape feedbacks are biologically distinct modeled channels. The original article explicitly displays a two-dimensional feedback surface but its analytical uniqueness and asymptotic results focus on the diagonal. Complete global parameter-wise uniqueness, exact monotonic prevalence response with a sharp sigma=1 zero-sensitivity boundary, and provably noncommensurate one-channel limits resolve the natural question of whether either channel alone creates SIS-like endemic prevalence. This determines precise immune-class residues and prevents interpreting a large single feedback as an SIS reduction. It does not rely on arbitrary finite slices or claim dynamical stability.
